data.title: Visa Moves to Close Credit Card Reward Loophole for Meme Token Purchases
data.description:
Visa is working to fix a loophole that allowed users to earn rewards when buying meme tokens with credit cards through Crossmint. According to Foresight News, the issue involved using merchant codes normally assigned to digital media, a category typically used for e-books, films, and music, which let cardholders receive standard credit card points or cash back.

Crypto in America said letters it reviewed showed Visa told at least one industry participant that the category was not appropriate for meme token purchases and informed processors, including Checkout.com, that the coding would no longer be accepted. Payment processors have been given a grace period to phase out the practice, which is expected to end next week. After that, such transactions must be treated as crypto asset transactions and will be subject to Visa's related restrictions.

data.title: South Korea Justice Minister Nominee Withdraws After Cabinet Reshuffle
data.description:
South Korea’s nominee for justice minister withdrew before confirmation, according to Bloomberg.

The pullout is the second ministerial nomination to be withdrawn in a week after the president reshuffled his cabinet.

data.title: Aptos Labs Launches Confidential APT on Mainnet
data.description:
Aptos Labs announced that Confidential APT has gone live on the Aptos mainnet. According to ChainCatcher, balances and transfer amounts are encrypted on-chain, while validators check zero-knowledge proofs to confirm transfers are valid without viewing the exact amounts.

Addresses remain public, and participation in the feature is entirely optional. The design allows public verification without public disclosure of transaction amounts.

data.title: TRUMP Token Team Address Transfers 11.25 Million Tokens, With 3.25 Million Moved to CEX
data.description:
TRUMP token team address transferred 11.25 million TRUMP 12 days ago, according to EmberCN monitoring cited by BlockBeats on September 19. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, 3.25 million of those tokens were further transferred to a centralized exchange, or CEX, 7 hours ago.

The report said the team address moved the tokens in a transaction valued at about $26 million, and the later transfer involved tokens worth about $6.9 million. It remains unclear whether the tokens will be sold.

data.title: AI TRENDS | TRM Labs Says YouTube Tutorials Lured Victims Into Deploying Crypto Theft Contracts
data.description:
Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said groups posted YouTube tutorials claiming to show how to build AI arbitrage bots with tools such as Claude, then guided victims to deploy and fund smart contracts themselves. According to Foresight News, the scheme did not rely on phishing links, spoofed domains, or malicious prompts, leaving victims to deploy theft contracts on-chain and weakening traditional interception signals.

TRM said that from February 2026 to August 2026, nine similar tutorials were linked to about 224 victims, with about 274.6 ETH flowing into six addresses. The videos often used AI-generated hosts and voiceovers, while the scripts and profit demonstrations were highly repetitive. Some tutorials directed users to fake compilation websites that replaced visible source code with malicious bytecode. The funds were then moved through DeFi, cross-chain bridges, and mixers.

data.title: YZi Labs Head to Join UN Digital Cooperation Day 2026 Panel on Tokenization and Public Infrastructure
data.description:
YZi Labs Managing Partner and Head Ella Zhang will join the panel “Blockchain and the Tokenized Future: Sovereign Choices and Safeguards for Next-Gen DPI” at UN Digital Cooperation Day 2026. YZi Labs posted on X.

The discussion will examine tokenization beyond digital currencies, including land, securities, and commodities, as well as how prepared countries are and what safeguards are needed before tokenized rails can be integrated into public infrastructure.

The panel is scheduled for Monday, 21 September, from 13:30–14:30 ET in New York. YZi Labs thanked @ODET_UN and @PakistanVARA for the invitation.

data.title: Linera Founder Says Project Will Stop Operations After Fundraising Falls Short
data.description:
Linera founder Mathieu Baudet announced on Discord that the project will stop operations immediately after its fundraising efforts fell short. According to PANews, Baudet said token sales on Sonar drew about $900,000 in subscription commitments, but the amount did not reach the minimum required to complete the sale, and all subscription funds have been returned to participants.

Baudet also said the team tried to raise emergency funding to keep operations running until mainnet launch, but it was unable to secure the needed capital. He said this ultimately led to the project’s closure. Earlier reports said Linera’s LNRA community round received 848,300 USDC in commitments, below the 1.5 million USDC minimum target, and would be refunded.

data.title: Radix Foundation Reports Exploit of Unseen Radix Engine Vulnerability
data.description:
Radix Foundation said an attacker used an undiscovered vulnerability in Radix Engine to withdraw assets from third-party vaults without owner authorization, then bridged them through Hyperlane to networks including Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Solana before selling them. According to Odaily, the flaw originated from a code cleanup in June 2023, and an independent security audit by Zellic in August 2024 did not detect it.

About three hours after the incident, Radix validators took enough stake offline to prevent the network from reaching consensus and stop further exploitation. The affected assets included ETH, WBTC, USDT, USDC, BNB, and SOL. Radix said the fix has been completed and independently reviewed and tested, and network recovery is now underway.

data.title: SEC Receives Amended S-1/A for 21Shares Injective ETF as Altcoin ETF Race Heats Up
data.description:
The SEC has received an amended registration statement for the 21Shares Injective ETF, moving the proposed fund a step closer to becoming a publicly traded product, according to Crypto Briefing. The amended S-1/A updates the original October 2025 filing and would give traditional investors regulated access to INJ, the native token of the Injective Network. If approved, the ETF would list on Nasdaq under the ticker TINJ, passively tracking INJ via the FTSE Injective Index, with a twist: discretionary staking of a portion of holdings to boost returns.

Structured as a Delaware statutory trust and sponsored by 21Shares US LLC, the fund's original S-1 landed on October 20, 2025, and the latest amendment keeps the registration active as the review continues. The preliminary prospectus notes shares have not traded publicly and no financial statements are included yet. INJ staking rewards ranged from 9.3% to 13.62% annually in 2025, giving the ETF a yield dimension most equity-focused products cannot match. As of September 1, 2026, INJ's circulating supply stood at about 92.8 million tokens, with a market capitalization near $488 million.

21Shares is no stranger to wrapping digital assets in traditional packaging, already offering a 21Shares Injective Staking ETP to European investors and having been among the first issuers of spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs via its ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF partnership. Since spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024 and Ethereum products followed later that year, asset managers have raced to file for funds covering Solana, XRP, Litecoin, Cardano and a growing list of layer-1 and DeFi tokens.

Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built on the Cosmos SDK for decentralized finance, focused on decentralized exchanges, derivatives and cross-chain trading. Its low-double-digit staking yield offers a tailwind pure price-tracking products can't replicate. The $488 million market cap is notable: for comparison, Bitcoin's is in the trillions and Ethereum's typically above $200 billion, so an INJ ETF drawing even tens of millions could represent a meaningful share of the token's float. The choice of the FTSE Injective Index — from London Stock Exchange Group's FTSE Russell — is also notable as the firm expands its digital-asset indexes, while custody arrangements remain unfinalized, a detail the SEC will likely want settled before any approval.

data.title: Trump Says Son Will Repay Wedding Party Costs Funded by Russian Oligarch
data.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said his son, Donald Trump Jr., told him he would repay a Russian oligarch who funded his May wedding celebration in the Bahamas. According to Sina Finance, Democratic lawmakers in Congress launched an investigation this week after reports said Russian businessman and International Boxing Association President Umar Kremlev paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the event. Trump told reporters on Friday that when he asked his son about the reports, Donald Trump Jr. replied, "Dad, I will pay the money back." A person familiar with the matter confirmed that Donald Trump Jr. plans to reimburse Kremlev.
